skill.name: container-hadolint
skill.description: Use this skill to run Hadolint checks on Dockerfiles, configure security-focused rules, add CI gates, and translate findings into remediation guidance.
skill.summary: Guides Hadolint-based Dockerfile security scans, CI integration, and remediation.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, reference URLs, taxonomy labels, and labeled Dockerfile examples. The real issue found is supply-chain exposure from downloading a latest Hadolint executable without checksum verification in the install guidance and CI template. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration intent, or malicious automation was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin a specific Hadolint release and verify its SHA256 checksum before chmod and execution. Prefer a pinned action version or container digest in CI.
Use NUL-delimited file discovery and quote all path variables so Dockerfiles with spaces or unusual names are handled safely.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Executable Download Without Checksum
semantic_findings.description: The install guidance and GitHub Actions template download the latest Hadolint binary from GitHub and make it executable without pinning a release or verifying a checksum. Users who copy these steps rely on mutable remote content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both locations contain direct download-and-chmod install steps for an executable. The risk is supply-chain exposure rather than evidence of malicious exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Insecure Dockerfiles can ship weak users, unpinned packages, and risky shell forms. This skill guides Hadolint scans, CI checks, and remediation for container builds.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to install and run Hadolint locally or through Docker.
Provides GitHub Actions and GitLab CI templates for Dockerfile linting.
Maps key Hadolint rules to container security and CIS Docker Benchmark concerns.
Shows configuration profiles for strict, balanced, and permissive linting.
Gives remediation patterns for common Dockerfile findings.
limitations: It does not scan built images for package CVEs or runtime vulnerabilities.
It cannot verify private registry policy without user-provided configuration.
Some examples require Hadolint, Docker, or CI permissions already installed.
Rule severity choices may need adjustment for legacy Dockerfiles.

use_cases.title: Review pull request Dockerfiles
use_cases.description: Check Dockerfile changes before merge and explain each Hadolint finding in plain language.

use_cases.title: Set CI quality gates
use_cases.description: Add repeatable Hadolint checks to GitHub Actions or GitLab CI with chosen failure thresholds.

use_cases.title: Map findings to controls
use_cases.description: Connect Dockerfile issues to CIS Docker Benchmark themes and practical remediation work.

prompt_templates.title: Scan one Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Dockerfile with Hadolint guidance. Explain the highest priority issues and give safe fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a lint policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hadolint configuration for production Dockerfiles. Use strict security rules and explain each exception.

prompt_templates.title: Add CI enforcement
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Hadolint checks to my CI workflow. Use a warning threshold and publish results for pull request review.

prompt_templates.title: Triage container findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Triage these Hadolint results by security impact, map them to CIS themes, and produce a phased remediation plan.

output_examples.input: A Dockerfile installs packages without version pins and runs as root.
output: High priority: add a non-root user for the runtime stage.
Medium priority: pin package versions or document approved exceptions.
Next step: rerun Hadolint with the production threshold after fixes.

output_examples.input: A team wants Hadolint checks in pull requests.
output: Recommended workflow: run Hadolint on each Dockerfile changed in the pull request.
Use a warning threshold for production branches and store reports as CI artifacts.
Review suppressed rules during security sign-off.

output_examples.input: A legacy image has many lint findings.
output: Start with root user, ADD usage, shell-form entrypoints, and hardcoded credentials.
Move style and image-size warnings into a later cleanup phase.

best_practices: Pin Hadolint versions and verify downloaded binaries before use.
Keep rule suppressions narrow and record the reason for each exception.
Combine Dockerfile linting with image scanning and secret scanning.
anti_patterns: Treating a clean Dockerfile lint result as a full container security review.
Disabling noisy rules globally instead of fixing or justifying each case.
Downloading CI tools from mutable latest URLs without checksum verification.

faq.question: Does this skill run Hadolint for me?
faq.answer: It provides commands, configurations, and CI templates. Hadolint must be available in your environment.

faq.question: Can it find vulnerabilities inside a built image?
faq.answer: No. Use an image scanner such as Trivy or Grype for package and runtime vulnerabilities.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: How should teams handle false positives?
faq.answer: Use a Hadolint configuration file, keep ignores specific, and document each accepted risk.

faq.question: Does it support CI integration?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes GitHub Actions and GitLab CI examples for automated Dockerfile linting.

faq.question: Is Hadolint enough for compliance?
faq.answer: No. It helps with Dockerfile controls, but compliance also needs policy, review, and runtime evidence.
